description: The experience around a product: the structure people navigate, the content and interface words they read, the components they use, and the service behind it all.

prerequisites: A current menu, page list or feature list for the product, and who uses it
first-value.starter-task: Restructure a menu users get lost in, and get the test that proves the new one works
first-value.starter-prompt: Our help centre menu has grown to 15 items and customers can't find refunds or delivery tracking. Current menu: Getting Started, Account, Orders, Shipping, Delivery, Returns, Refunds, Payments, Gift Cards, Promotions, Membership, Privacy, Terms, Contact Us, Community. Design the information architecture and the tree test to validate it.
first-value.verification: information-architecture returns an inventory with a keep/merge/cut status for every item, a sitemap tree and a Mermaid diagram that match, a label rationale table, findability risks for refunds and tracking, and tree-test tasks that don't use the menu's words.
first-value.recovery: If you get a journey map instead, ask for it by name ("use information-architecture"). If labels look invented, give it your search terms or support ticket themes and ask it to tag every label's evidence.

journey.when: You're designing or fixing the experience around a product or service: how it's organised, what it says, how its components behave, and what happens behind the scenes.
you_bring: who the users are and their top tasks
the current menu, page list or feature list
existing page text, screenshots or wireframes for the flow you're working on
your design tokens or brand kit, if you have one
what you know about the teams and systems that deliver the service

steps.you_do: Hand over the content or feature list and the users' top tasks.
steps.you_get: A sitemap and nav model with a label rationale table, findability risks, and a tree-test plan.
steps.decide: Run the tree test before building, or accept the structure as a hypothesis.

steps.you_do: Pick a key page from the sitemap and give it the current text or the facts it must contain.
steps.you_get: User-need statements, the questions in priority order, a plain-language draft with a before/after readability check, and a cut list.

steps.you_do: Give it the flow's screens or steps and your voice.
steps.you_get: A string table with budgets and variants for every button, label, error and empty state, plus a terminology list.

steps.you_do: Name a component the flow needs and your token set.
steps.you_get: A component spec with anatomy, every state by token, keyboard and ARIA behaviour cited to WCAG 2.2, and open questions for engineering.

steps.you_do: Describe one customer scenario and what you know about the teams and systems behind it.
steps.you_get: A blueprint table and Mermaid diagram with fail points, waits, pains traced to causes, and 2–3 ranked fixes.

steps.you_do: Run it on any of the specs before you share them.
steps.you_get: A verdict and severity-tagged findings with a fix for each.

journey.you_end_with: A tested-or-testable structure, the content and strings for a key page and flow, a buildable component spec, and a service blueprint with the fixes ranked.
